subject: On‑prem key handoff criteria and egress controls for private deployment
messages:
From: Sara Mullins <sara@orbitalhealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, procurement@orbitalhealth.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy – key custody + egress constraints

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options last week. Before we move to a technical review, Procurement and Legal have asked for a concise write‑up of the following items so they can confirm internal approvals:

1) Who will hold the customer keys (customer KMS vs. Redwood managed keystore) for an on‑prem/VPC install?
2) If Redwood maintains operator access for upgrades/troubleshooting, what are the minimum privileges and what telemetry/logs would be accessible to Redwood?
3) Any scenarios that could trigger cross‑border transfer of telemetry or model telemetry outside the US?
4) Example contractual language around breakglass/escrow access and notice windows.

If you can send a short summary and any checklists or templates you have, we can circulate internally. Attaching our baseline requirements if helpful.

Appreciate it,
Sara
Sara Mullins
Director, IT Security
Orbital Health
- Attachment: OH_private_deploy_baseline.pdf (pdf)

From: lauren.bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mullins <sara@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, marucs.lin@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy – key custody + egress constraints

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. I've summarized our typical options below and attached a short checklist that maps to each ask. High level: Redwood supports three patterns for private deployments (VPC or on‑prem) with progressively tighter customer control:

A) Customer‑managed KMS (recommended for regulated customers) — customer provisions and manages keys in their cloud KMS or on‑prem HSM. Redwood components are configured to use the customer KMS; we do not store plaintext keys.
B) Customer keystore with Redwood operator handshake — customer holds root keys; Redwood holds an encrypted keystore for runtime with keys only unwrapped within customer‑controlled boundary. Operator activities require a signed breakglass request plus 2‑party approval.
C) Redwood managed keystore (not for regulated workloads) — Redwood hosts keys; SLA and access controls apply as in our standard DPA.

Telemetry and operator access:
- We only collect heartbeat and anonymized service metrics by default. Debugging traces that include request identifiers are stored in customer logs only when explicitly enabled.
- Operator access (when permitted) is scoped and audited. We propose RBAC with time‑boxed elevated sessions and 30‑day notice post‑incident except for active security incidents where immediate access may be needed (we still provide rapid post‑access audit).

Cross‑border transfers:
- We will not route customer data or request payloads outside the region you specify for the deployment. Non‑PII service telemetry (errors, perf metrics) can be aggregated to our central observability in the US; we can opt‑out on a per‑customer basis.

I've attached a one‑page checklist and a draft clause set for DPA/escrow language. Can we book a 30‑minute call with your legal and procurement tomorrow to align on small edits?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Privacy Programs
Redwood Inference
- Attachment: redwood_onprem_key_handshake_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- Attachment: draft_dpa_key_clause_v3.docx (docx)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private deploy – key custody + egress constraints

Lauren / team — adding technical detail for (A) and (B) above so Procurement can vet operational impact.

- Customer‑managed KMS (A): we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and standard PKCS#11 HSMs. Keys never leave the customer HSM; we use an envelope encryption approach. Runtime agents fetch wrapped keys via customer‑controlled endpoints.
- Customer keystore with operator handshake (B): operator actions require a signed request recorded in the audit log plus an HSM‑mediated unseal. We propose the following minimum controls:
  * Dual authorization for unseal (operator + customer security rep)
  * Time‑limited unseal token (max 12 hours)
  * Full session recording (logs stored in customer log sink)
  * Automatic rekey after any privileged session

Telemetry egress:
- By default, system health pings (service up/down, GPU metrics) can be sent to Redwood; payloads with any customer data are explicitly disabled.
- For on‑prem installs we provide a toggle to keep all diagnostic snapshots local; remote support then uses a secure remote session brokered by the customer's security team.

I'll be available on the call and can share a short diagram of the handshake flow.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private deploy – key custody + egress constraints

Folks — adding suggested contractual language and small policy changes we should surface to Orbital's counsel. Key points to call out to Legal: 

1) Breakglass / Escrow:
- We propose an escrow addendum: Redwood will only access keys in a true emergency (defined: active compromise of production environment or legal order). Access requires (a) documented customer approval path or (b) judicial/administrative process. All accesses are recorded and subject to independent audit quarterly.

2) Access windows and notice:
- For planned maintenance or support: 48 hour notice + customer authorization.
- For security incidents: immediate access allowed but Redwood will provide detailed incident report and audit within 72 hours.

3) Subprocessors and data flow:
- Any subprocessors used for diagnostics or orchestration will be listed in the DPA; for on‑prem installs we will minimize subprocessor usage and default to customer‑only endpoints when required.

4) Data localization:
- Add an explicit clause that workload payloads and customer prompts are not transferred outside the designated region. Telemetry summary metrics only if customer opts in.

I'll attach a redline of the DPA clause and a short checklist of evidence items Orbital's auditors often request (SOC2 reports, change controls, operator access logs).

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Counsel
Redwood Inference
- Attachment: draft_dpa_key_clause_v3_redline.docx (docx)

From: Sara Mullins <sara@orbitalhealth.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@orbitalhealth.com>, Annette Lopez <annette.lopez@counsel.co>, rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy – key custody + egress constraints

Lauren / team — this is helpful, thank you. A few quick clarifications from Legal & Procurement after an initial read: 

• Orbital prefers pattern (A) where we keep root keys. Please confirm you can support PKCS#11 HSMs behind our firewall and that you will not cache unwrapped keys.
• On operator breakglass: we will require dual‑party approval (Redwood engineer + Orbital Sec Ops) for any unseal. The 12‑hour max token duration looks good, but Procurement wants the token expiry to be configurable by Orbital with a 6–24 hour window.
• Please send the redline you mentioned and a one‑page evidence checklist (SOC2, personnel background checks, incident playbook) we can hand to our auditors.

Can you get those items to Annette (cc'd) and schedule the 30‑minute call for tomorrow at 10am PT if that works for your team?

Sara
Sara Mullins
Director, IT Security
Orbital Health
